question_text: A 26-year-old woman with poor prenatal care and minimal antenatal screening presents to the emergency department in labor. Shortly thereafter, she delivers a baby girl who subsequently demonstrates symptoms of chorioretinitis on examination. A series of postpartum screening questions is significant only for the presence of multiple cats in the mother’s household. The clinical team orders an enhanced MRI examination of the infant’s brain which reveals hydrocephalus, multiple punctate intracranial calcifications, and 2 sub-cortical ring-enhancing lesions. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
